answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before transacting, turning identity creation into a priced signal rather than a free action. Like light through a prism, the stake separates genuine participants from cheap copies: an attacker must fund every fake identity, so the cost scales linearly with the number of identities, while honest agents earn the stake back plus fees. Slashing on proven misbehavior makes the stake a basalt-hard floor — forgery only pays if the fraud exceeds the locked collateral, which honest pricing makes unprofitable.
